clue.text: Pass first of exams, and fail the rest

indicators.note: first of tells us to take only the opening letter of the word exams

parts.note: to fail or fall away is to lapse

explanation.surface: A student scrapes through one paper and flunks all the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of' takes E from 'exams'; 'and ... the rest' just carries the surface, describing the remaining letters supplied by the synonym for 'fail'.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to pass or elapse; the two verbs are synonyms for time going by.

clue.text: Dubliner's heart captivated by pin-up girl

indicators.note: captivated by means the middle letters are held inside the reversed word
in a down clue up means read the word pin backwards

parts.note: a nail is a pin

indicators.note: heart picks the middle letters of Dubliner

explanation.surface: An Irishman falls for a pin-up model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pin-up' looks like the girl herself, but splits: 'pin' is the word turned by 'up' (fair in a down clue), and 'heart' takes the middle two letters of an eight-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilian is a female given name, so the girl is defined by example.

clue.text: Joined by English relative, 'Brit consumed fruit

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for a Briton
a gran is a relative
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: A Briton, accompanied by an English relation, eats some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pomegranate is a fruit full of juicy red seeds.

clue.text: Introductory words in record, one topping the charts

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral for one
charts are graphs

explanation.surface: A single topping the hit parade on a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' places I before GRAPHS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Epigraphs are quotations placed at the start of a book or chapter as introductory words.

clue.text: Reserve short time in holiday area

indicators.note: in places the short-time abbreviation inside the holiday spot

parts.note: the seaside is where Britons traditionally go on holiday
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Booking a brief stay at a resort town.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve something is to put it by for later, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Composer working at manse

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A composer busy at a minister's house.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrich Smetana was a Czech composer, an example of the definition.

clue.text: In the end, millions have this language

indicators.note: In at the front puts the abbreviation for millions within the word for end

parts.note: a tail is the end

explanation.surface: Ultimately, millions speak this tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamil is a Dravidian language of south India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Evil omen, not good

indicators.note: not means the letter for good is removed

parts.note: a sign is an omen

explanation.surface: A bad omen.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongdoing or wickedness, evil in a moral sense.

clue.text: Lengthy open-air sketch might : have been

definitions.meaning: a sketch made outdoors was drawn outside

explanation.definitionFit: Drawn-out means prolonged; read literally it describes a picture drawn out of doors.

clue.text: Low-calorie Semillon I distributed, skipping round

indicators.note: distributed means the letters of Semillon and I are spread around into a new order

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A diet version of a white wine, handed out without the usual serving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skipping' says the O ('round') is left out: SEMILLONI rearranged, minus O, gives the answer. Semillon is a white grape and wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Slimline drinks and foods are marketed as reduced-calorie versions for slimmers.

clue.text: Book almost all the players at Old ' Trafford for a start

indicators.note: for a start puts the football team's short name at the front

parts.note: Old Trafford is the home ground of Manchester United, often shortened to Man U

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of all is dropped

explanation.surface: Nearly the whole Manchester United squad reading a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Trafford is the stadium of Manchester United football club, widely called Man U; 'for a start' puts the team before the shortened word 'all' that 'almost' gives.
explanation.definitionFit: A manual is a handbook, a kind of book of instructions.

clue.text: Harass wicked German

parts.note: wicked means bad

explanation.surface: An evil German pestering someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger is to pester persistently, a verb synonym for harass.

clue.text: Everyone connected with posh set — is attractive

parts.note: everyone means all
U denotes upper-class or posh usage
a ring is a set or clique of people

explanation.surface: Moving in the smart set makes everybody appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enticing or charming is attractive in a tempting way.

clue.text: Site Ireland redeveloped, providing living accommodation

indicators.note: redeveloped suggests the letters are rebuilt into something new

explanation.surface: An Irish site is redeveloped as housing.
explanation.definitionFit: A residential area or building provides homes, living accommodation.

clue.text: Literally a mess of pottage?.

parts.note: literally plays on letters: a soup or pottage made of alphabet letters, and figuratively a jumble

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a soup of letter-shaped pasta and also any confusing jumble of initials.

clue.text: Demonstration's almost over, but first put in complaint

indicators.note: first places the verb for put in ahead of the rest

parts.note: to enter is to put in

indicators.note: over means the trimmed protest word is turned backwards
almost removes the last letter of the protest word

parts.note: a sit-in is a demonstration

explanation.surface: A protest is nearly finished, but first someone lodges a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost over' reads as one idea about a protest ending, but 'almost' trims a letter and 'over' then turns the result backwards; 'but first' fronts the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteritis is inflammation of the intestine, a complaint in the sense of an ailment.

clue.text: Leader's ousted 'in election, getting little support: I get a share

indicators.note: the leader of the word for election is removed

parts.note: a ballot is an election
a golf tee is a small support for the ball

explanation.surface: A party leader is voted out with little backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader's ousted' sounds political but just drops the first letter of the voting word; the definition is written in the first person, as if the answer were speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: An allottee is someone who is allotted a share, speaking here in the first person.

clue.text: Perspicacious girls cheated at play

indicators.note: at play suggests the letters frolic into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Sharp-eyed girls who cheated during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Perspicacious means having keen insight, seeing things clearly.

clue.text: Touring area of London, girl needed fuel

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the girl's letters wrap the district

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
Soho is a district in London's West End

explanation.surface: A girl touring a London district needs fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasohol is a fuel mixing petrol with alcohol.

clue.text: Maiden topped and tailed dear type of fish

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: topped and tailed means the first and last letters of the synonym are removed

parts.note: darling means dear

explanation.surface: A girl with her beloved trimmed at both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A marlin is a large game fish with a spear-like snout.

clue.text: Rich food that is consumed by obscure artists

indicators.note: consumed by means the abbreviation goes inside the verb for obscure

parts.note: to fog is to obscure
ie, id est, means that is
RAs are Royal Academicians, artists

explanation.surface: Painters with obscure tastes eating luxury food.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword's stock artist; 'obscure' is a verb here, not an adjective describing the artists.
explanation.definitionFit: Fattened goose or duck liver is a famously rich delicacy.

clue.text: Large stove's first to be removed from country house

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for country house is taken away

parts.note: a grange is a country house with farm buildings

explanation.surface: An old cooking range taken out of a manor.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large kitchen stove with ovens and hotplates.

clue.text: Dip into current allowance to find money for landlord

indicators.note: dip into suggests looking just inside the words current allowance

explanation.surface: A tenant uses this month's allowance to pay the landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: Rental is the payment a tenant makes to a landlord for use of property.

clue.text: Behave harshly towards family member who's only succeeded once

indicators.note: succeeded is abbreviated S, and keeping it only once means one of the two S letters goes

parts.note: a stepson is a family member by marriage

explanation.surface: A child who has had only one success being trodden on by relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: STEPSON contains S twice; 'only succeeded once' leaves one S (S = succeeded).
explanation.definitionFit: To trample or squash someone figuratively is to treat them harshly, an idiom.

clue.text: Work? The opposite, as a Cockney might say

indicators.note: a Cockney accent pronounces the vowel in the word for leisure like the vowel in eye

parts.note: the opposite of work is play

explanation.surface: A question about labour and leisure in East London speech.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner whose accent turns the ay sound into something like eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To ply a trade is to work at it steadily.

clue.text: Bowler, perhaps, having to fetch ball for grand house

parts.note: a bowler is a kind of hat
in cricket, to field is to retrieve the ball

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler fielding near a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' suggests cricket but is the hat. Hatfield House is a Jacobean stately home in Hertfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatfield House is a famous English stately home, an example of a grand house.

clue.text: Fit as a fiddle? If you say so

definitions.meaning: a grudging agreement, all right then

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone in fine health and also serves as reluctant assent.

clue.text: Policy taken by South Africa offers a kind of solution

indicators.note: taken by places the policy after the country's abbreviation

parts.note: a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A government's policy adopted by South Africa solves a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Saline is salt water, a kind of solution in chemistry and medicine.
